sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A supply cart has 5 boxes with 4 markers in each box and 2 loose markers. Which expression represents the total number of markers?
A library has 8 shelves with 13 books on each shelf. Then 36 books are loaned out. How many books remain?
In 463544, how does the value of the 4 in the ones place compare with the value of the 4 in the tens place?
choices: 10 times as much
the same value
100 times as much
1/10 as much

items.prompt: Round each number to the nearest hundred to estimate 5111 - 1874.
Round 150 to the nearest hundred and 85 to the nearest ten, then multiply to estimate the product.
A student says 98 × 42 = 4116. Round each number to the nearest ten. Which choice correctly checks the claim?
choices: The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 3990.
The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 4010.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 4116 and the rounded estimate is 4000.
The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 4000.

items.prompt: A student evaluates 6 × [12 + (15 - 6)] + 8: “They multiply 6 by 12 first, then finish the calculation, so the value is 89.” Which statement best identifies the error?
choices: The student multiplied before evaluating (15 - 6); the innermost difference is 9, giving 134.
The student used the right first step but made an arithmetic slip; the value should be 136.
The first error is in the final addition or subtraction; the value should be 135.
The work is correct; 89 is the value.

items.prompt: A student says, “In 6914439, the value of the 4 in the hundreds place is the same value as the value of the 4 in the thousands place.” Which statement best analyzes the error?
choices: The values are 400 and 4000; 400 is 1/10 as much as 4000, so the student's comparison is incorrect.
The values are 400 and 4000; 400 is 10 times as much as 4000.
The values are 400 and 4000; 400 is the same value as 4000, so the student's comparison is correct.
The places are adjacent, so 400 is 100 times as much as 4000.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Which expression means: “Multiply 3 by 2, then subtract the product from 50.”
Which phrase describes 62 + [8 × (14 - 10)] without evaluating it?
choices: Subtract 10 from 14, multiply the difference by 8, then add 62.
Add 14 and 10, multiply the sum by 8, then add 62.
Multiply 8 by 14, add 62, then subtract 10.
Subtract 10 from 14, add 8, then multiply the sum by 62.

items.prompt: Let E represent 2059 + 8865. Without evaluating, how does 5 × (2059 + 8865) compare with E?
choices: 4 times as large as E
5 times as large as E
5 greater than E
6 times as large as E
